deep.reconstruction:
Context (folio 12v/13r). This is the manuscript of Riemann's student-era study 'Versuch einer allgemeinen Auffassung der Integration und Differentiation' (dated 1847). It was published posthumously in the Gesammelte Werke (1876, ed. Weber/Dedekind). Riemann writes Π(s) for Gauss's factorial, so Π(s)=Γ(s+1).

On the previous page he expands z(x+h) in a generalized Taylor series: z(x+h)=Σ_μ h^μ/Π(μ)·p_μ. Each coefficient is p_μ(x,k)=Σ_{n≥0} z^{(n)}(k)(x−k)^{n−μ}/Π(n−μ). The coefficient of h^μ/Π(μ) is the x-derivative of the coefficient of h^{μ−1}/Π(μ−1), so p_μ is taken as 'a value of ∂_x^μ z'. Differentiating in k telescopes: dp_μ/dk = −z(k)(x−k)^{−μ−1}/Π(−μ−1). For μ<0 every term of p_μ vanishes at k=x.

This page.

(7) Integrating dp_μ/dk from x to k gives
p_μ = ∫_x^k −z(κ)(x−κ)^{−μ−1}/Π(−μ−1) dκ = (1/Π(−μ−1)) ∫_k^x (x−t)^{−μ−1} z(t) dt.
In modern notation this is (1/Γ(−μ)) ∫_k^x (x−t)^{−μ−1} z(t) dt, the Riemann–Liouville integral of order −μ with lower terminal k. It is valid when z is continuous between k and x and μ<0, so that the exponent −μ−1>−1 and the integral converges at t=x.

Applying the same formula to the coefficient of order μ−n (also negative) gives the value belonging to the same expansion:
∂^{μ−n} z = (1/Π(n−μ−1)) ∫_k^x (x−t)^{n−μ−1} z(t) dt.

Change of base point. Different choices of k give different expansions of z(x+h) and different values of ∂^μ z, but they belong to 'one system'. Replacing k by k_1 adds
(1/Π(−μ−1)) ∫_{k_1}^{k} (x−t)^{−μ−1} z(t) dt.
Expanding (x−t)^{−μ−1} binomially in powers of t/x (my step: binom(−μ−1,n) = Π(−μ−1)/(Π(n)Π(−μ−1−n))) gives
Σ_{n=0}^∞ x^{−μ−1−n}/Π(−μ−1−n) · ∫_{k_1}^{k} (−t)^n/Π(n) z(t) dt.

Since z is continuous between k_1 and k, every integral is a finite constant independent of x. So the ambiguity in ∂_x^μ z is a series Σ K_n x^{−μ−1−n}/Π(−μ−1−n) with arbitrary constants K_n. This is Riemann's 'complementary function'; the next page writes it as Σ_{n≥1} K_n x^{−n−ν}/Π(−n−ν).

The red marginalia ('∂_x^μ z', 'besonderen Zeile!') are later editorial or typesetting marks, apparently for the 1876 edition: notation changes and instructions to set formulas on separate lines.
errors: The binomial expansion of (x−t)^{−μ−1} in powers of t/x converges only if |t|<|x| for all t between k_1 and k. Riemann does not state this; in general the difference is an analytic function of x near x, not globally such a power series.

The term-by-term identification of p_μ with the k-integral assumes the generalized Taylor series and its k-derivative converge, and that term-wise differentiation is allowed. These are formal steps, not justified on the page.

The resulting 'complementary function' with arbitrary constants is the known weak point of Riemann's theory. It was criticized by Cayley (1880) because the operator then lacks a clean index law. This is a conceptual issue rather than an algebraic slip; the algebra itself is correct.

results.what: For μ<0, ∂_x^μ z = (1/Π(−μ−1)) ∫_k^x (x−t)^{−μ−1} z(t) dt, derived from a generalized Taylor expansion of z(x+h)
results.modern_name: Riemann–Liouville fractional integral (with arbitrary lower terminal)
results.usually_credited_to: Abel (1823), Liouville (1832); this form with general terminal named after Riemann (1847 MS, publ. 1876); Sonine/Letnikov (1868–69)

results.what: Changing the lower terminal k→k_1 changes the fractional integral by Σ x^{−μ−1−n}/Π(−μ−1−n)·c_n with constants c_n (via binomial expansion)
results.modern_name: Riemann's complementary function / terminal dependence of Riemann–Liouville operators

deep.surprise_reason: This is the manuscript of Riemann's known posthumously published 1847 paper on generalized differentiation. The Riemann–Liouville integral and the complementary function are already attributed to him from exactly this text.

checkable.asserts: Riemann–Liouville integral of order 1/2 (μ=−1/2) of t^2 from k=0 equals Γ(3)/Γ(7/2) x^{5/2}; result 0 (assume x>0)
Binomial coefficient identity used in the expansion, with Π(s)=gamma(s+1); result 0
Telescoping dp_μ/dk = −z(k)(x−k)^{−μ−1}/Π(−μ−1) for μ=−1/2, z=exp, up to the truncation remainder; result 0
Semigroup check: two half-integrals from 0 equal one full integral for z=t; result 0

transcription_corrections: In (7) the left integrand carries a minus sign: ∫_x^k −z_(k)(x−k)^{−μ−1}/Π(−μ−1) dk. The transcription dropped the '−'.
The parenthetical condition reads 'und μ negativ ist'; this is consistent with −μ−1>−1 on the previous page.
In the struck formula after ∂^{μ−n}z, the original reads ∫_k^x (x−t)^{−μ+n} z_t dt (an abandoned version without −1); the main formula has exponent −μ+n−1.
'dass zu verschiedenen dem k verschiedenen Werthe giebt' should be read as 'dass, je nachdem man dem k verschiedene Werthe giebt, verschiedene Entwicklungen von z(x+h) daraus hervorgehen'.
The red marginal note at top right reads approximately '∂_x^μ z ∂_x^μ z' (a notation substitution mark), not '∂_z^μ z'.
